_comment: Content of the dialog that asks to confirm the workflow chosen in the Wizard (question 2), and captions of the Wizard help images. 'captions' maps an image file (relative to biapy/wizard/) to its caption, used wherever the image appears. Each workflow has 'name', 'description' (HTML) and 'blocks' shown in order. A block is one of: {'text': HTML}, {'images': [{'file', optional 'caption'}], 'width'} (one row of images), {'note': HTML} or {'shared': key} (inserts the blocks of shared[key]). In any HTML, '{ref:key}' cites references[key]: it becomes a number like [1] and the reference is listed at the end. 'docs' is the link to the workflow's documentation.

references.backova: Backová, Lenka, et al. "Modeling Wound Healing Using Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoders and Transformers." 2023 IEEE 20th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI). IEEE, 2023.
references.biosr: F-actin images of the BioSR dataset by Qiao et al.: https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/BioSR/13264793.
references.n2v: Krull, Alexander, Tim-Oliver Buchholz, and Florian Jug. "Noise2Void - Learning Denoising From Single Noisy Images." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2019.
references.trackastra: Gallusser, Benjamin, and Martin Weigert. "Trackastra: Transformer-based cell tracking for live-cell microscopy." European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV), 2024. Bacteria data: van Vliet et al., Cell Systems, 2018.

sem_inst_det.note:
Semantic segmentation, instance segmentation or detection? Semantic segmentation gives all the objects of the same class the same label, so objects of the same class that touch or overlap cannot be separated from each other. If you need each object on its own, choose:
  • Detection, if you only need to locate the objects (e.g. to count them).
  • Instance segmentation, if you also need a mask of each object, e.g. to measure its size or shape (morphological properties).

sem_inst_det.text: The difference is easy to see in a natural image, processed here with each of the three workflows:

SEMANTIC_SEG.name: Semantic segmentation
SEMANTIC_SEG.description: The goal of this workflow is to assign a class to each pixel (or voxel) of the input image, producing a label image with semantic masks. The simplest case is binary classification: only two labels are present in the label image, black pixels (usually with value 0) are the background and white pixels the foreground (usually labeled with 1 or 255).

INSTANCE_SEG.name: Instance segmentation
INSTANCE_SEG.description: The goal of this workflow is to assign a unique ID, i.e. an integer value, to each object of the input image, producing a label image with instance masks. Each object gets its own value, even when it touches other objects of the same kind.

blocks.note: Tracking. If your images are the frames of a time-lapse, this workflow can also track the objects over time: it segments each frame and links the objects of consecutive frames, so each one keeps its number along the time-lapse and cell divisions are detected. The wizard asks about it next.

DETECTION.name: Detection
DETECTION.description: The goal of this workflow is to localize objects in the input image, without a pixel-level mask. Common strategies produce either bounding boxes containing the objects or individual points at their center of mass, which is the one adopted by BiaPy.

blocks.text: This is an example of this workflow:

DENOISING.name: Denoising
DENOISING.description:
The goal of this workflow is to remove noise from the input images. BiaPy can learn it in two ways:
  • Self-supervised, with Noise2Void {ref:n2v}: only the noisy images are needed. This is very useful because clean images are frequently unavailable.
  • Supervised, if you also have a clean (noise-free) version of each noisy image to use as target. The Wizard will ask you about it.

blocks.text: This is an example of this workflow:

SUPER_RESOLUTION.name: Super-resolution
SUPER_RESOLUTION.description: The goal of this workflow is to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) ones. When the HR image is bigger than the LR one by a scale factor (x2, x4), the task is known as single-image super-resolution.

blocks.text: This is an example of this workflow:

CLASSIFICATION.name: Classification
CLASSIFICATION.description: The goal of this workflow is to assign a label to each whole image, not to its pixels.

blocks.text: This is an example of this workflow:

IMAGE_TO_IMAGE.name: Image to image
IMAGE_TO_IMAGE.description: The goal of this workflow is to translate input images into target images of the same size, e.g. to predict one imaging modality from another, like fluorescence from brightfield. It is like super-resolution but without upsampling (scale factor x1).

captions.semantic_seg_collage.png: Left: confocal image of a Drosophila embryo recovering from a laser-incised wound (input). Right: its semantic mask, the contour of the wound {ref:backova}.
captions.confirm/semantic_seg_gt.png: Its semantic mask: mitochondria (white, foreground) and background (black).
captions.instance_seg_collage.png: Left: electron microscopy image (input). Right: its instance mask, where each color is a different mitochondrion.
captions.detection_collage.png: Left: fluorescence microscopy image of nuclei (input). Right: the detected nuclei, each one marked with a red dot {ref:jukkala}.
captions.denoising_collage.png: Left: noisy fluorescence image (input). Right: its denoised version {ref:convallaria}{ref:n2v}.
captions.sr_collage.png: Left: low-resolution fluorescence image (input). Right: its high-resolution version, x2 {ref:biosr}.
captions.classification_collage.png: Dermatoscopic images of skin lesions, each one assigned to a class {ref:medmnist}.
captions.i2i_collage.png: Left: brightfield image (input). Right: the paired fluorescence image where the nuclei are highlighted (target) {ref:lightmycells}.
captions.confirm/sem_inst_det_workflow_diff.jpg: Top left: original image. Semantic segmentation (top right): one mask per class, dog (red) and sheep (blue); the three sheep merge into a single region. Detection (bottom left): each animal is located, here with a box (BiaPy marks the center of each object with a point instead), but its shape is not delineated. Instance segmentation (bottom right): each animal has its own mask, even where they overlap {ref:sheep}.
captions.confirm/instance_seg_multichannel.gif: Instances with classes. Left: histology image (input) from the CoNIC challenge {ref:conic}. Right, alternating: its label image with the instance masks (channel 0) and with the class of each instance (channel 1).
captions.tracking_bacteria.gif: Bacteria tracked by Trackastra: the path of each cell over time (time goes up), with its links in green when correct, magenta when wrong (false positives) and cyan when missed (false negatives) {ref:trackastra}.
